description: Framework-agnostic UI components built on modern web standards. Most components are plain CSS over native HTML; the rest are Light-DOM custom elements, used only where keyboard coordination, focus management, or state synchronisation cannot be expressed accessibly in CSS.
rules: Timeless has two kinds of component, configured differently. CSS components are a native element with a `ui-*` class, configured with `data-ui-*` attributes: `<button class="ui-button" data-ui-variant="primary">`. Custom elements are a registered `ui-*` tag, configured with plain attributes and never `data-ui-*`: `<ui-tabs orientation="vertical">`.
Never write a CSS component as a custom element. `<ui-button>` does not exist; it is `<button class="ui-button">`.
Boolean attributes are presence-based. Author `invalid`, never `invalid="true"` or `data-ui-invalid="true"`.
Component anatomy is authored by the consumer and marked with a whitespace-separated `data-ui-part` token list, selected with `[data-ui-part~='name']`.
Never author `data-ui-internal-*` attributes. They are private runtime hooks.
Native HTML semantics, ARIA, and platform pseudo-classes are authoritative for state. Do not add state classes, and do not use ARIA to replace behavior a real element provides.
Timeless wires relationships, never content. Accessible names are always the consumer's to supply.

Import stylesheets from `@timelessui/components/css/<file>` and register custom elements from `@timelessui/components/define/<tag>`. `tokens.css` is required once by every component. Registration is per-element and explicit.

The full contract for any component — permitted attributes and values, parts, state, custom properties, element API, and canonical markup — is at `https://timeless.build/docs/components/<component>.md`. The index is at `https://timeless.build/llms.txt`.
